title: The Quiet Minute
credit: Built on Robert's preview rewrite (preview-stories-e4e6722). Lines and reflections revised for a first-time player.

intro.kicker: Student union · 9:40 pm · the room is booked until ten
intro.text: You chair the committee planning tomorrow's welcome walk for two hundred new students. Tonight the route has to be agreed. Theo has already decided what it is.

cast.name: Nia
cast.role: walked the route today and found a problem

cast.name: Theo
cast.role: designed the route and built the model; proud of it

cast.name: Ellis
cast.role: has drawn another route; hasn't shown anyone

prompt: Twenty minutes of room left. How will you make room for what you haven't heard?

setup.speaker: Theo
setup.line: Main gate, the courtyard, then down to the harbour just as the lights come on. That's the moment. That's what they'll remember.
setup.direction: proud and warm, a little too fast, selling an idea he loves

setup.speaker: Nia
setup.direction: careful, trying to get a word in

setup.speaker: Theo
setup.line: Is a great photo stop, I know. Ten minutes there, tops.
setup.direction: cheerfully talking over her, not noticing

setup.speaker: Nia
setup.line: No, I mean it's locked. After six. I checked today.
setup.direction: quietly firm, slightly hurt at being talked over, trying to stay calm

setup.speaker: Theo
setup.line: Security will open it if we ask. It'll be fine.
setup.direction: breezy, dismissive without meaning to be, hand staying on the model

setup.line: Nia looks down at her map. Ellis has a folded sheet under one hand, and hasn't said a word all evening.

setup.speaker: You
setup.line: Twenty minutes left, and I've only really heard one person.

round.speaker: You
round.line: Let's go round once. One concern each, and nobody replies until everyone's spoken. Nia, you first.

round.speaker: Nia
round.line: The courtyard gate locks at six. If we start there at half five, it's still open, and we're not stuck outside with two hundred people.
round.direction: relieved to be heard, steadier and clearer now

round.line: Theo opens his mouth, then remembers the rule. He waits.

round.speaker: Ellis
round.line: That's where mine starts, actually. The courtyard. But it never reaches the harbour. I know that's the part you love, Theo.
round.direction: hesitant, then braver; gentle with Theo

round.speaker: Theo
round.line: It is. Show me your first stop.
round.direction: a beat of disappointment, then honest and open

round.line: Someone knocks: the next group needs the room. Everyone has spoken. The route isn't finished, and the harbour is off the table for now.

slips.speaker: You
slips.line: Everyone, write down one thing that worries you about tomorrow. No names. Then we'll read them together.
Pens scratch. Theo writes one too. The slips come back: gate locked after six. Too crowded at the harbour. A different start?

slips.speaker: You
slips.line: So the courtyard's the problem. We drop it?
slips.direction: reading quickly, decisive, a little too fast

slips.speaker: Nia
slips.line: No, don't drop it. The courtyard's where I met my first friend here. I want them to see it. Just go there first.
slips.direction: stung, then open and honest; it matters to her

slips.speaker: You
slips.line: Sorry. I read that too fast. Courtyard first.
Ellis unfolds the sheet at last. The route almost fits. One slip still says too crowded, and you don't know who wrote it.

lesson: Fix the room, not just the person: the format you choose decides who gets heard.

round.title: You gave every voice a turn.
round.kept: Nia finished her point, and Ellis spoke for the first time all evening.
round.cost: Time. The room ran out before a plan, and Theo's harbour finale is gone for now.
round.ask: Who might still stay quiet, even in a round?

slips.title: You let people write before they spoke.
slips.kept: Everyone had a say without fighting for the floor, Theo included.
slips.cost: Writing loses tone. You misread Nia's note, and one worry has no owner.
slips.ask: How would you find whoever wrote 'too crowded'?
